messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: streaming-api p99 spike detected across eu-west-2 and us-east-1. Multiple streaming stalls, increased TLS handshake retries, SLO breach (p99 > 3s). Paging oncall (team: runtime+network). Runbook: streaming-tail-latency.

pjensen: Acked. Oncall here. Seeing alerts + dashboard graphs. p95 at ~800ms, p99 > 4.2s for streaming RPCs. Error rate for streaming sessions up ~2%. Investigating.

afigueroa: I see concurrent path changes in the VPC route tables in eu-west-2 around the start time, and ECMP counters spiked. Possible re-ordering/packet duplicate. Also see MTU fragmentation logs in the edge NAT.

mchoi: Streaming runtime shows a bunch of retransmits and TLS renegotiations in logs. KV cache miss rate jumped 30% which will amplify tail tokens. Correlating session IDs now.

afigueroa: tcpdump from nat-gw-17 shows lots of out-of-order packets and dup ACKs. Suspect asymmetric routing + ECMP on a subset of hosts.

pjensen: Quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce batch size on streaming workers to reduce egress burst. 2) force single-path routing for problematic subnets (route tweak) in eu-west-2. 3) enable short-lived local cache warm (kv warm) for high-rate clients. Who can execute 2?

afigueroa: I can push a route policy to pin next-hop for the affected /22 to a single AZ peer for the next 15m. Doing it now (will monitor).

mchoi: I’ll flip the streaming batch config from 64->16 for canary hosts to measure tail. Pushing a canary change to 10% of streaming fleet now.

lgarcia: Support: Which customers are affected? I'm seeing 3 customers with increased complaints (voice transcription and live chat). Drafting a short notification.

sbenedict: Paging escalation: if SLO still breached in 10m -> page infra lead. Also opening a ticket for post-incident RCA.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T12:14:02Z by mchoi -> streaming-worker-config: batch_size=16 (canary 10%). Status: started.

pjensen: Running tcpdump + quick checks. Commands used:```sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -n -s 96 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0 and port 443' -w /tmp/streaming-handshake.pcap``` and ```ss -tanp | grep ESTAB | wc -l```

afigueroa: Route pin applied to eu-west-2 /22 -> next-hop azb-peer-3. Monitoring ECMP counters. Initial drop in re-ordering metrics by ~40%.

mchoi: Canary batch change rolled. Early signal: p99 on canary hosts down from 4.2s -> 1.1s. Global p99 still high because only 10% changed.

pjensen: Good. Next step: expand batch change to 50% if ECMP pin holds. Also runtime to warm kv cache aggressively for top N clients to reduce token generation tail.

afigueroa: Network note: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion observed on nat-gw-17 (port-util ~92%). We're seeing retries when a new TLS connection tries to allocate ephemeral port and gets a RST from overloaded SNAT. I'm reducing connection TTL and enabling ephemeral port reclamation.

mchoi: On runtime side I can enable connection keepalive pooling and KV warm for the most active session keys. Doing that now for the canary cohort.

lgarcia: Customer message drafted: "We're investigating increased latency for live streaming in EU and US. Engineers have applied routing mitigations and are rolling runtime config changes. We'll follow up with impact details and ETA to fully mitigate." Want to send once we confirm canary improvement.

pjensen: Can we get a quick list of affected customer IDs and recent traces? mchoi: pulling traces and correlating session IDs -> list in 1m.

mchoi: Found correlation: clients making lots of small connections (short-lived TLS sessions) are disproportionally hit. That plus SNAT port pressure explains the handshake spike. Attaching sample trace IDs: trace-44A1, trace-44A2, trace-44B7.

afigueroa: Implemented ephemeral port reclamation and lowered conn TTL at the NAT for eu-west-2. Watching for reduced TLS SYN retries.

sbenedict: If TLS retries drop and p99 improves within 10m, we'll keep rolling. If not, escalate to infra lead @infra-lead.

pjensen: Observability: add a temporary dashboard panel showing SYN retransmit rate, out-of-order packets, NAT port-util, and streaming p99 by AZ.

mchoi: KV warm completed for top 50 session keys in canary. Also enabled keepalive pooling. Early traces show fewer TLS handshakes and fewer new TCP flows.

afigueroa: NAT port-util down to ~65% after reclamation. ECMP re-ordering metrics down ~60% after pinning.

mchoi: Canary expansion to 50% started. deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T12:22:34Z by mchoi -> streaming-worker-config: batch_size=16 (canary 50%).

deploy-bot: deploy completed -> streaming-worker-config 50% canary.

lgarcia: Sending customer notification now.

lgarcia: Message posted to affected customers. Support channel updated.

pjensen: Monitoring global p99: dropped from 4.2s -> 1.3s over 12 minutes. Streaming stall incidents count decreasing. Continuing to watch for next 30m.

sbenedict: Marking incident as mitigated if metrics hold for 30m. Open action items: RCA (network asymmetry + NAT port tuning), long-term fix: increase SNAT scale or add ephemeral port pool + implement smarter connection pooling in runtime.

afigueroa: I'll follow up with a change to avoid ECMP across AZ boundaries for streaming egress prefixes.

mchoi: I'll work on a runtime change to prefer connection reuse and graceful backpressure to avoid bursts.

lgarcia: We'll follow up customers with root-cause summary and timelines.

pjensen: Great work everyone. If alerts re-fire, re-open this thread. Otherwise I'll start the post-incident doc. :thumbsup:
